page: Microsoft Azure D64pls_v5 is a compute-focused general purpose virtual machine powered by an Ampere Altra processor based on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core) clocked at 3.0 GHz. The configuration allocates 128.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration supporting standard AES instructions.

The virtual machine does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on remote premium storage capabilities. Network configurations omit complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark testing reveals a clear performance profile typical of high-density ARM architectures: multi-threaded scaling is a core strength, as evidenced by top-quartile results in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing (112,418.18) and high throughput in software compilation via Clang (46,168.0) and ray tracing tasks (52,174.0). Memory systems demonstrate high cached read throughput reaching 4,383.1 GB/sec in 16 KB block benchmarks, while Redis SET operations achieve strong performance at 80.12 million operations per second.

A notable tradeoff lies in single-threaded performance. Single-core Geekbench scores register in the bottom quartile at 1,124.0, accompanied by lower text processing results and average single-threaded compression speeds. Uncached large-block memory operations fall into average percentiles, with 177.02 GB/sec read and 76.69 GB/sec write bandwidth. Extended instruction sets such as x86 AVX and AMX are absent due to the ARM architecture.

Cost efficiency is driven by the resource density of the Ampere ARM cores and the lean 2:1 memory-to-core ratio, which avoids overhead for workloads that do not demand extensive memory footprints. Microsoft Azure D64pls_v5 is appropriate for scalable multi-threaded workloads, including software build farms, Clang CI/CD compilation pipelines, containerized microservices, ray tracing jobs, and in-memory key-value caching such as Redis.
description: Microsoft Azure D64pls_v5 is an ARM64 virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated Ampere Neoverse-N1 physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz, coupled with 128.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU). The instance contains no bundled local storage or GPUs, utilizing remote storage for persistence. Benchmark results indicate top-quartile multi-threaded compute efficiency, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core result of 112,418.18, high Clang software compilation throughput (46,168.0), and 80.12 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core processing capabilities trail behind, reflected in a lower Geekbench single-core score of 1,124.0. The configuration lacks x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX-512. Microsoft Azure D64pls_v5 offers favorable cost efficiency for compute-dense workloads with modest per-core RAM requirements, making it well fitted for parallel software compilation, CI/CD runners, containerized backend services, and distributed caching systems.
